name: Carcassonne
edition: 20th Anniversary Edition (2021) rulebook; core rules only, fields and farmers are in a separate supplemental sheet

key_numbers.label: Meeple in your supply
key_numbers.value: 7 (the 8th sits on the score track at 0)

key_numbers.label: City
key_numbers.value: 2 points per tile and per coat of arms

setup.text: Put the start tile (darker back) in the middle of the table.
Shuffle the other tiles and place them face down in several stacks that everyone can reach. For a first game, leave out the 17 river tiles and the 15 anniversary mini-expansion tiles.
Put the scoreboard beside the play area. Return unused meeple colours to the box, and for a first game the 5 abbots too.
Choose a colour. Take 7 meeple of it as your supply, and put the 8th on the 0 space of the scoreboard.
The youngest player goes first. Play clockwise.

turn.summary: Place a tile, optionally place one meeple on it, then score anything you completed.
steps: Draw 1 face-down tile and place it face up touching a tile already on the table, so roads, cities and fields continue.
You may place 1 meeple from your supply on the tile you just placed, as a traveller on a road, knight in a city or monk on a monastery, if no meeple is already anywhere on that connected feature.
Score every feature your tile completed. Move your scoring marker forward and return the meeple of each scored feature to its owner's supply.
If you cannot legally place the drawn tile, return it to the box and draw another.

end: The game ends when all tiles are placed and a player cannot draw and place one on their turn. Then do final scoring of incomplete features.

scoring.text: Completed road (both ends closed, or looped): 1 point per tile in it.
Completed city (fully walled with no gaps): 2 points per tile and 2 more per coat of arms.
With several meeple on a scored feature, the player with most meeple takes all points. Tied players each take the full points.
End of game, incomplete road: 1 point per tile. Incomplete city: 1 point per tile and per coat of arms. Incomplete monastery: 1 point per tile including itself and the surrounding tiles.
End of game, each field scores 3 points per completed city next to it. Fields and farmers are explained only in the supplemental sheet.

tiebreak: None is given: the player with the most points wins.

missed.text: You may only place a meeple on the tile you just placed, never on an older one.
You cannot place a meeple on a feature that already has any meeple on it, even if it is far along the same road or city. Two meeple can end up together when a later tile joins two separate features.
A completed feature scored by someone else's tile still scores for you. Only features completed on the current tile are scored on that turn.
Meeple leave the board only when their feature is scored. A meeple on an unfinished feature stays, and does not return to your supply.
Monasteries are in the centre of a tile, so a monastery tile must continue the surrounding landscape like any other.
Incomplete cities score half at the end: only 1 point per tile and shield, not 2.

not_covered: Fields and farmers: placing and scoring are in the supplemental rulesheet, which was not read.
River tiles, abbots and the 20th anniversary mini-expansion.
unverified: Player count 2 to 5: the rulebook text only shows 5 meeple colours and does not print a player range.
